ops.text: Indemnification. HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (1) an allegation that the Site or any services or deliverables provided by HDI infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (2) HDI's breach of applicable law; (3) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of the Company's data or Content caused by HDI; or (4) HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The Company shall defend and indemnify HDI against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of Content provided by the Company or the Company's breach of applicable law. The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of any such claim, the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim, and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense.

verification.notes: The finding of "missing" is corroborated: the rendered original text (Sections 8, 9, 10.8) contains no cap, no exclusive remedy and no consequential-damages exclusion, so a concise insertion is the correct instrument. Fallback checklist is complete on the face of new Section 10.9: a mutual aggregate cap on a 12-month fee basis with confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence and willful misconduct expressly outside the cap. Position-complete at fallback. Preferred is not reached: missing the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, the mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion, and the data protection/security, fraud and IP-infringement carve-outs, plus the statement that Company payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. These are the exact operative additions required to move to preferred. Minimality holds: a single new subsection is added, nothing existing is deleted or paraphrased, no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no extra damages categories, no procedure and no carve-outs beyond the four fallback elements. Numeric threshold is not exceeded (no volunteered USD floor). Intent preserved: Section 10.9 is additive, sits after 10.8 in General Provisions, introduces no undefined term ("Company" and "Party" are existing usages), creates no dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict the Warranties or Confidentiality articles. Drafting nit for the file, not a defect: the cap is anchored to "the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" rather than the preferred "preceding the event giving rise to the claim"; this is acceptable at fallback but should be corrected if we push to preferred.
